what: Goshains are included among Faqirs; "followers of Shankaracharya" and divided into ten classes, most common Gir, Puri, Bharthi, Ban; split into householders who marry and strict celibates living in small maths, who always travel in pairs
quote: Among the Faqirs are included the Goshains ... They are followers of Shankaracharya and are divided into ten classes, of which the most common are those known as the Gir, Puri, Bharthi, and Ban.

what: Goshains held in high esteem, all castes drink water from their vessels; recruited from all but the lowest orders; bury dead sitting with salt
quote: The Goshains are held in high estimation, and all castes will drink water from their vessels, although their ranks are recruited from all save the very lowest orders of society.

what: Goshains great traders; formerly monopolised hill trade in jewels, gold, spices, drugs; celibacy prevents dispersion of property
quote: The Goshains are great traders, and many of them have acquired much wealth; in former days they monopolized the trade in jewels, gold, spices, and drugs from the hills.

what: Bharthi (Bharati) mahant of Itara among chief Goshains
quote: Among the chief Goshains are the Bharthi mahant of Itara, and the Ban mahant of Srinagar, in pargana Gonda.

what: Ban mahant of Srinagar; village lands 593 acres (Rs 900) held by Goshains; village 688 persons mostly Kurmis
quote: lands cover 593 acres, assessed at Rs. 900 and held by Goshains.

what: Of villages, Goshains own 34, Nanakshahis 20 (a single estate), Bairagis 12; Bairagis and Goshains also hold shares in other villages
quote: Goshains own 34 villages, Nanakshahis 20, which form a single estate, and Bairagis twelve.

what: Of villages: twelve each by Goshains and Nanakshahi faqirs, two by Bairagis
quote: twelve each by Goshains and Nanakshahi faqirs, ten by Banias, three each by Kurmis, Kayasths, and Khattris, two by Bairagie

what: Three villages held by Goshains; single zamindari villages shared with the wealthy Mahant of Chhapia
quote: three by Goshains, one by Kurmis

what: Goshains hold 7 villages (one pargana), 9 villages (Utraula pargana), 3 villages (Tarabganj-type), single zamindari villages partly Goshains with property in Basti, 2 mahals (Guwarich), 12 mahals incl. Goshains
quote: seven by Goshains, five by Muraos, and one by Europeans.

what: Bairagis hold one village and nine mahals, Goshains two mahals
quote: Bairagis hold one village and nine mahals, Musalmans four villages and six mahals, Goshains two mahals

what: Raja of Khurasa granted 250 bighas around Gaureshwar Mahadeo temple to Gorkhi Gir, Goshain, who cleared jungle and built the village; one of four mahals still with his descendants; about 200 Goshains in population of 660
quote: The Raja of Khurasa made a grant of 250 bighas of land surrounding this temple to one Gorkhi Gir, Goshain, who cleared the jungle and built the village.

what: Gaureshwar Mahadeo temple retains local sanctity; Holi pilgrimage
quote: The temple still possesses considerable local sanctity, and pilgrims come here in large numbers during the Iloli festivals.

what: Temple visited by pilgrims whose offerings go to the resident Goshains
quote: pilgrims, whose offerings are given to the resident Goshains.

what: Italian-style house adjoining the palace built by Moti Gir, Goshain, wealthy merchant; Goshains numerous in this part, formerly smuggling jewels from Nepal
quote: This was built by one Moti Gir, Goshain, a wealthy merchant. The Goshains are numerous in this part of the country, and in former days are said to have been extensively engaged in smuggling jewels from Nepal.

what: Temple of Bhagwan Gir, Goshain, east of the town on the Fyzabad road beside the chilbil tree; recent construction
quote: notably those of Mihin Lal, Khattri, and Bhagwan Gir, Goshain, in the east of the town along the Pyzabad road

what: Saint Ganga Gir Goshain credited with miraculous birth of Datt Singh and planting the chilbil tree bound up with fortunes of the Gonda raja's house
quote: through the miraculous intervention, it is said, of the celebrated saint, Ganga Gir Goshain, who planted the famous chilbil tree at Gonda

what: Tank sacred to Dukharan Nath Mahadeo built over a century ago by a Goshain of Balrampur; two other Goshain [temples] close by
quote: This was built over a century ago by a Goshain of Balrampur; it stands in a picturesque garden, and close by are two other Goshain

what: Lingam discovered by a Goshain during the Mutiny; temple Karauhan Nath rebuilt; Sheoratri fair of ~20,000
quote: During tho Mutiny a lingam was discovered here by a Goshain, and further excavations disclosed an old well and a few small images.

what: Sheoratri fair about 20,000 attendees at Karauhan Nath
quote: A large fair attended by some 20,000 persons is held here annually on the Sheoratri.

what: Mahant Har Charan Das, Nanakshahi faqir, successor of Mahant Gur Narain Das (gift and purchase before annexation); Basantpur estate in Gonda: 12 villages and 8 mahals, 8,682 acres in pargana Gonda plus 5,890 acres Paharapur etc.; Court of Wards in minority
quote: He is a Nanakshahi faqir and the successor of Mahant Gur Narain Das, by whom the property was acquired by gift and purchase shortly before annexation.

what: Nanakshahi villages (20) form a single estate (Basantpur)
quote: Nanakshahis 20, which form a single estate

what: Shrine of Swami Narain (Sahajanand; adopted by Ramanand of Junagarh) with Vaishnava brotherhood of four orders: Brahmacharyas, Sadhus, Palas and lay disciples; Mahant of Junagarh is proprietor of the village; Vaishnava (Swaminarayan), not Dasnami
quote: the shrine of Swami Narain and the religious brotherhood attached to it

what: Wealthy Mahant of Chhapia shares single zamindari villages with Munshi Prag Narain
quote: shares the single zamindari villages with the wealthy mahant of Chhapia

what: Temple at Debi Patan: third building raised by Ratan Nath, third in descent from Gorakh Nath, founder of the Jogis (14th cent.); ~20 mahants of Debi Patan have presided over the brotherhood of Kanphata Jogis; Aurangzeb's officer slew the priests
quote: Since Ratan Nath there have been some twenty mahants of Debi Patan, who have presided over the brotherhood of Kanphata Jogis, so called from the great round earrings that they wear.

what: Chait fair (1st to 9th of light half) attracts about 75,000 pilgrims and traders; sacrifices of buffaloes, goats, pigs; Nepal hill pony trade
quote: The fair is held from the 1st to the 9th of the light half of Chait and attracts some 75,000 pilgrims and traders.

what: Mahant Jagjiwan Das of Kotwa, founder of the Sattnami sect, secured release of Guman Singh and gave him his daughter in marriage
quote: the celebrated Mahant Jagjiwan Das of Kotwa in Bara Banki, who was the founder of the Sattnami sect and a person of great influence.

what: Beni Madho Das, disciple of Tulsi Das, wrote the Goshain Charitra (Goshain = Tulsidas, Vaishnava)
quote: Beni Madho Das of Paska was a disciple and companion of Tulsi Das, whose life he wrote in the form of a poem entitled the Goshain Charitra.

what: Banjaras and Nagas (low tribe or ascetic class unclear) in tradition of desolation
quote: Banjaras and Nagas ; so great was the desolation
